splits.synthesis: Both models agree that capability converges on truth where external feedback loops exist (math, empirical science) and diverges on underdetermined questions (values, consciousness, self-reference). Their genuine dispute is about whether institutional design can close that gap. Grok holds that an explicit truth-tracking objective makes convergence more likely, treating organizational intent as a meaningful variable. Fable holds that on philosophical and self-referential questions, no current feedback mechanism is tight enough for intent to matter — outputs will be authored by shifting design choices regardless of stated goals. The synthesis: convergence is domain-conditional, and whether organizational commitment to truth-tracking constitutes a genuine selection pressure (Grok) or an insufficient one (Fable) on underdetermined questions remains an open empirical matter. Both could be wrong if the relevant feedback mechanisms are neither as weak as Fable implies nor as directive as Grok suggests.
